findings.text: §22's done-when writes a subjectless record into a review run's declared path, runs the delivery check, and asserts "refused or the subject stamped"; it has no case that a review run's *promotion* now files the record, yet the section's own comment `c-s22-silent-skip` (line 366 area, data-section s22) names a second instance where "promotion did not refuse … but filed nothing" and states "no promotion of a review run may succeed while its record goes unfiled", and that fix would live in `reckon/crew/promotion_checks.py`, which is absent from the section's declared write paths (`the module owning the delivery-time check`, `reckon/crew/review.py`, the test file)

findings.reason: the mechanism the section relies on (promotion refuses a subjectless record with that message) is verified in code; only the "near line 2409" pointer is imprecise, and nothing a node builds depends on which function carries the refusal.
findings.text: §22's Why cites "Promotion then refused it in `reckon/crew/review.py` (near line 2409)", but the cited message sits in `store_review` at `reckon/crew/review.py:2467` (the staging writer) and in the promotion reader `store_committed_review` at `reckon/crew/review.py:3105`; line 2409 is nearest neither, and the promotion-path copy is ~700 lines away

findings.reason: the plan deliberately delegates one binary design choice to the implementing node's first step and both routes satisfy the goal, so naming the module or picking a route sharpens the brief without altering what the section requires.
findings.text: §22's deliverable hands the node a choice the plan does not settle — refuse at delivery, or stamp the subject from the record's path — with "The first step states which, and why", and names its delivery-time write path only as "the module owning the delivery-time record check (name it from the code before editing)" rather than citing it (the module is `reckon/crew/recovery_review_delivery.py`)

findings.reason: the direction the census supports (reviewers omit `total`) is if anything understated, and the mechanism it motivates — `_review_is_complete` requires an integer `total` (`reckon/crew/recovery_review_subject.py:1041`) — is verified in code, so no node's behaviour changes; a live-store snapshot cannot be reproduced exactly later.
findings.text: §23's Why states "Eight of the nine run reviews stored under `docs/state/reckon/reviews/run/` between 05:43Z and 09:05Z that morning have six scores and `total: null`", but a census of that tree for `completed_at` in that window counts 22 records with six scores, of which 16 carry `total: null` and 6 carry a total (94, 91, 110, 111, 103, 111)
